name: Joshua Rotenberg
company: Denver Center for the Performing Arts
body: I'm applying for the Associate Director of Digital Marketing role. I live in Arvada, so the on-site expectation is a short drive rather than a relocation question, and the DCPA is a landmark in a city I've worked in for most of my career.

The part of the posting I'd point to first is the distinction between strong platform performance and meaningful business performance, because most of my work sits on that line. At Level Agency I led integrated strategy across paid media, inbound, and content, and built the reporting frameworks that tracked ROI, CAC, LTV, and conversion behavior for quarterly reviews with client leadership. At Solenzo I run a Google Ads account where the platform numbers looked acceptable and the leads did not: I rebuilt targeting and negatives to cut the spam, then traced the remaining gap to the site's conversion path rather than calling the campaign fixed on click quality. That is the same reasoning your live-campaign monitoring and vendor accountability sections describe, applied at a smaller scale than a touring Broadway campaign.

On the leadership side, I managed and developed a team of onboarding specialists at Wix, contributed to hiring and training for a brand-new vertical that went from proof of concept to a profitable business line, and built sales training used by tenured account executives. Cross-functional influence without direct authority has been most of my career, first as the person advising executives and external partners, now as a founder. I'll be straightforward that my background is B2B and agency rather than ticketed live entertainment, so revenue pacing against a show calendar would be new context, though the underlying question of whether digital activity is actually moving sales is not.

One more reason this role interests me: I spend my working days building AI and agent systems, which has given me a practical view of how generative models retrieve and surface content. Your posting names generative engine optimization as something to lead into rather than something to worry about, and I'd like to help work that out with your team. I'd welcome the conversation.
